papers.title: A Survey of Robotic Navigation and Manipulation with Physics Simulators in the Era of Embodied AI
papers.summary: Navigation and manipulation are core capabilities in Embodied AI, but training agents to perform them directly in the real-world is costly, time-consuming, and unsafe. Therefore, sim-to-real transfer has emerged as a key approach, yet the sim-to-real gap persists. This survey examines how physics simulators address this gap by analyzing properties that have received limited attention in prior surveys. Deceptive sequential decision-making via regularised policy optimisation
papers.summary: Autonomous systems are increasingly expected to operate in the presence of adversaries, though adversaries may infer sensitive information simply by observing a system. Therefore, we present a deceptive sequential decision-making framework that not only conceals sensitive information, but actively misleads adversaries about it. We model autonomous systems as Markov decision processes, with adversaries using inverse reinforcement learning to recover reward functions. papers.title: Graph transformers and stabilized reinforcement learning for large-scale dynamic routing modulation and spectrum allocation in elastic optical networks
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has been widely applied to dynamic routing, modulation, and spectrum assignment (RMSA) in optical networks, yet no prior work has trained a transformer model for this task. We attribute this to the high data and compute requirements of transformers and potential training instabilities with RL. papers.title: Bridging Humans and Technology Through Touch - Human-Centered Haptic Technologies for Tactile Perception, Sensorimotor Augmentation, and Industrial Assistance
papers.summary: The sense of touch is the only human sense that requires physical contact, linking together perception and action in a closed sensorimotor loop that no other modality can fully replicate. Yet the gap between human haptic capability and what engineered systems can measure, transmit, or reproduce remains wide. This thesis investigates how haptic technologies can be designed to acquire, transmit, amplify, and exploit human tactile perception, in order to improve interaction with remote environments, robotic systems, and industrial processes. papers.title: GPS Monitor
papers.summary: GPS (Global Positioning System) location mapping is an inherent feature of many modern devices, including navigation systems, smartphones, and tracking devices. A GPS-capable device typically includes an off-the-shelf module that handles low-level GPS processing tasks such as satellite signal detection, latitude and longitude calculations, and other related computations. Given their relatively low cost and ease of use, GPS modules are often incorporated into maker projects such as DIY robots, model cars, and drones.

Demonstrations of automated vessels, mooring systems, and robotic cargo handling, supported by digitalisation in ports and freight centres, highlight significant potential. However, a structured methodology to evaluate the logistics performance of such innovations remains missing, as their translation into logistics practice and systemic impact are not fully comprehended. papers.title: Modeling Robot Head-Direction Duration and Switching Frequency During Side-by-Side Walking with a Human
papers.summary: Recent advancements in robotics have led to extensive research on social robots capable of moving alongside humans. However, existing studies on mobile robotics have largely overlooked head-direction behavior in the context of side-by-side interactions during walking. As an initial step toward addressing this gap, the present study investigated human head-direction behavior during side-by-side conversational walking. papers.title: Autonomous Robots Enabling Smart, Data-Driven Railway Maintenance
papers.summary: Railway transport is essential for sustainable mobility, but increased utilization accelerates infrastructure wear, raising maintenance demands that must be met without compromising availability or cost-efficiency. Emerging technologies in digitalization, AI, and robotics offer promising solutions, yet flexible, on-track inspection systems remain underexplored. This paper presents the development of lightweight, rail bound Multi-Purpose Inspection Robots (MPIRs) designed as research platforms for autonomous data acquisition in railway environments. Two prototypes are currently being developed

papers.summary: Safety and reliability play a crucial role when designing Robotic Autonomous Systems (RAS). Robots are increasingly operating beyond factory settings. However, in fields, orchards or poly-tunnels, robots are exposed to a different set of challenges. papers.summary: Needle placement in spine interventions is critical for effective pain management, yet it depends on reliable identification of anatomical landmarks and careful trajectory planning. Conventional imaging guidance often relies on both computed tomography (CT) and X-ray fluoroscopy, exposing patients and staff to high doses of radiation while providing limited real-time 3D feedback. papers.summary: Due to imbalances in global trade, shipping containers frequently accumulate in regions where they are not immediately needed, while other regions experience shortages. This mismatch forces shipping companies to engage in costly repositioning efforts to balance container supply. papers.title: Three methods, one problem: classical and AI approaches to no-three-in-line
papers.summary: Background The No-Three-In-Line problem asks for the maximum number of points that can be placed on an n × n grid with no three collinear, representing a famous problem in combinatorial geometry. Methods We compare three approaches: (i) integer linear programming (ILP) using Gurobi, (ii) transformer-based pattern learning via PatternBoost, and (iii) reinforcement learning using proximal policy optimization (PPO). papers.title: A Brief Tutorial on Reinforcement Learning: From MDP to DDPG
papers.summary: Following the evolution from theoretical foundations to advanced deep learning algorithms, a coherent overview of reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed in this tutorial. We begin with the mathematical formalization of sequential decision-making via Markov decision processes (MDPs). In MDPs, the Bellman equation and the Bellman optimality equation play important roles; they provide the basis for policy evaluation and the fundamental condition for optimal behavior, respectively. papers.title: Uncovering Latent Phase Structures and Branching Logic in Locomotion Policies: A Case Study on HalfCheetah
papers.summary: In locomotion control tasks, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated high performance; however, the decision-making process of the learned policy remains a black box, making it difficult for humans to understand. On the other hand, in periodic motions such as walking, it is well known that implicit motion phases exist, such as the stance phase and the swing phase.
